Puts it in the strip down the homepage, "On the tray this week". Tick as many as you like — the six newest show.

column1: THE CATEGORY CODES — the two letters in the Product Code
Jadauco menu → Check the catalogue. It runs the same rules the publish runs, and it can
read the Drive folder, so it catches the photo mistakes too:
· a filename in Images that is not actually in Drive — it names the file that IS there
· the same photo used by two different products
· a photo sitting in Drive that no row uses
Every cell at fault turns red with the reason in a note. Hover to read it.
Jadauco menu → Clear the check marks removes the red once you are done.
A clean check means the publish will go through. That is the whole point of it.
· Never change a Product Code once it has published. The code IS the product — changing it
does not rename anything. It deletes the old product and its web address, and creates a
new one. To move a piece to another category, delete its row and add a new one.
· Deleting a row deletes the product and its page. The sheet keeps its own version history
(File → Version history), so putting the row back and publishing again restores it.
· Never rename a column header — the website finds columns by their exact text.
· Never move the headers off row 1.
· Never type in Category (auto) — it is worked out for you.
· Renaming a product changes its heading, never its web address. That is deliberate — it protects the Google ranking.
· This sheet is readable by anyone with the link. No cost prices, no supplier names, no customer data.
